D.t: Phil Weiser leads by 21.5 in the forecast and wins 100% of simulations. The cushion is about 609,198 votes; a one point swing is about 14,187 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +12.2 and D +30.3. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Denver, a projected net 231,992 votes; Boulder, a projected net 116,072 votes; Arapahoe, a projected net 100,437 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: El Paso, even, 11.8% of the vote; Douglas, D +1.9, 7.1% of the vote; Pueblo, D +2.4, 2.7% of the vote; Garfield, D +10.5, 1.0% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Phil Weiser runs furthest behind in Weld, Pueblo, Boulder. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 82% of voters, 56 to 41, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.09 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 73% of voters, 59 to 38, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.67 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 61% of voters, 60 to 37, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.07 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Phil Weiser: Immigration voters 28 to 69, Small counties 46 to 50, Midsize counties 49 to 47. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$725K cash against $158K. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.
